title: Sisters in Sweat
tagline: Building the brand strategy, voice and visual identity for a fitness community from the ground up.
context: I joined Sisters in Sweat as a Marketing Executive. Soon after starting, it was clear there was a lot more ground to cover than the title suggested — there was no dedicated marketing team in place, and most of it was falling to me alone.
problem: Without a brand strategy in place, our visual language across social media and every other touchpoint had become incoherent — and beyond strategy, there was no visual identity or brand guideline deck to work from either.
process: I built trackers and systems that improved day-to-day efficiency and cut down the time spent in meetings. When I raised the gap in brand strategy and visual identity, we decided to build it in-house rather than bring in an agency — I owned and executed that project end-to-end, delivering a full brand guideline deck. I also led the brand marketing charter, handling collaborated brand campaigns across partners including Cava, Nike, Mille, Nykaa Wellness and In Her Interest by Zerodha.
outcome: Sisters in Sweat now runs on a brand system built entirely in-house — one consistent visual identity across every partner collaboration, and systems in place that keep the team's time focused on the work itself rather than admin. The content strategy work also helped solidify the Nykaa Wellness partnership and brought another protein brand on board.
carouselBody: Built the brand strategy, visual identity and marketing systems for a fast-growing wellness community — entirely in-house.

title: Mohmani
tagline: Creative strategy for an up-and-coming homegrown jewellery brand.

image.alt: Mohmani Instagram grid and brand world

context: Mohmani is a small, homegrown jewellery label that specialises in one-of-one pieces and custom orders. Over time, it has grown into a content and culture-heavy brand, shaped as much by the founder's personal voice as by the jewellery itself. Through viral content, events and word-of-mouth discovery, the brand has built a niche following of around 3.3k people who connect with its whimsical world.
problem: As Mohmani became more visible, the challenge wasn't reach — it was coherence. With the brand evolving across content, pop-ups and personal brand, there was a real risk of it feeling scattered or performative. The need was for clearer creative direction that could hold all of this together, without forcing the brand into a conventional lifestyle or commercial mould.
process: The focus was on putting some structure in place so creative decisions didn't feel random. Early on, the brand's core cues — whimsy, quirk, and subcultural references — were clearly defined and used to guide everything. Basic direction was set for visuals, tone, and a content calendar so posting stayed consistent and intentional. Each collection started with a clear inspiration, which was shared with the audience through creative concepts and content instead of long explanations. Content pillars were built around the jewellery itself, the making process, everyday moments, and the founder's personal voice, so the brand felt natural and expressive rather than over-produced. Over time, engagement, pop-ups, and viral moments were looked at to understand what resonated and refine the direction while staying true to the brand's niche.
outcome: Mohmani now feels more settled in its identity — less like a brand chasing growth, and more like one that has found its place. The creative strategy helped bring clarity and continuity across content, community moments, and product storytelling, while keeping the brand's quirks intact. It also gave the founder a flexible framework to keep experimenting, growing, and showing up authentically without losing what makes the brand resonate.
carouselBody: Creative direction and content strategy for a homegrown jewellery label balancing whimsy with commercial growth.

title: Voucher Management System
tagline: Conceptualising and leading end-to-end development of a voucher management system.
context: At Talview, a client-facing voucher system needed a clear owner to take it from concept to shipped feature.
problem: Vouchers were being handled ad hoc, with no consistent framework for issuing, tracking or documenting them for clients or internal teams.
process: Led end-to-end development of the voucher management system, from concept through to release. Wrote detailed release documentation and user-facing guides, and ran a competitive analysis of industry tools to build a framework for positioning and storytelling, supporting the product marketing team.
outcome: The system contributed to a 5% improvement in retention, and demonstrated end-to-end ownership from concept to release documentation.
carouselBody: Owned end-to-end development of a client-facing voucher management system, from concept to release.
